cim: Trump rejects 'globalist regulation' of artificial intelligence at APEC summit
cim_eredeti: Trump rejects 'globalist regulation' of artificial intelligence at APEC summit
szoveg_eredeti:
US President Donald Trump has declared that Washington firmly opposes any "globalist regulation" designed to control or restrict artificial intelligence, describing the emerging technology as "almost completely good" whilst conceding that it carries potential hazards.

"We oppose any form of globalist regulation or anything to control or stifle SI, and we won't allow that to happen, frankly," Trump said on Thursday during his keynote address at the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, using his preferred acronym "SI", or superintelligence.

"The United States is also proud to be the world leader in superintelligence, the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution," he told assembled delegates.

Acknowledging the dual nature of rapid technological advancement, Trump underscored the necessity of domestic vigilance rather than multilateral constraints.

"It's super intelligence, but we have to watch it. We have to be careful. We have to cherish it," he said. "It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements, and we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements."

Trump utilised the forum to highlight American economic growth and promote expanding US fossil fuel exports across the Asia-Pacific region.

He cited his administration's formal approval of an Alaska liquefied natural gas pipeline intended to export natural gas to Asian energy markets.

The president also revealed that American energy conglomerates are aggressively re-entering South America following political shifts in Caracas.

"We're doing tremendous business in Venezuela," Trump stated, noting that US oil firms are actively "moving in" to develop reserves.

Trump confirmed he would convene later in the day with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the summit, characterising the scheduled three-way talks as "a historic trilateral meeting" to "discuss more opportunities for all three."
